Section 11.1, printed pp. 245-246 (PDF pp. 253-254), gives a textbook nondegenerate adiabatic approximation. Corrected the reference and explicitly distinguished it from a quantitative gapped-subspace theorem; the model Definition and its local evolution and spectral prerequisites are unchanged.

The amplitude is defined as exp(i E_b(t-s)/hbar) times the Schroedinger matrix coefficient. The decomposition gives the latter coefficient exp(i(s E_a-t E_b)/hbar)<U_I phi_a,phi_b>; multiplying the defining phase gives exactly exp(is(E_a-E_b)/hbar), as clause (e) states. The rejection omitted the amplitude definition; no item edit is licensed by this false positive.

The compact interval permits a=b, whereas the norm Dyson supplier restricts derivatives to a<b. Added the same endpoint convention without removing singleton algebraic or norm conclusions, and treated U(a,a)=I explicitly in step 1.1. Also corrected step 1.2: the exp(K tau)-1 estimate comes from F1, not substitution N=0 in F2; corrected the Teschl attribution to autonomous evolution.

Clauses (a)-(c) asserted strong derivatives on an allowed singleton although proof 1.1 correctly made no such assertion. Made the Statement match the model and supplier endpoint convention, defined L=0 for a=b, and separated the singleton in proof 2.1. The graph bound, domain invariance and all nondegenerate strong claims remain intact. Corrected source titles that attributed nonautonomous and forced-oscillator theorems to autonomous textbook sections.

The declared compact interval need not contain the pi-pulse or return time: I=[0,1] seconds, s=0 and Omega1=1/second is a counterexample to unconditional evaluations. Qualified those evaluations by s+tau in I and periodicity by both elapsed times in I-s. The exact propagator and Rabi population formulas, including the zero-coupling case, are preserved. Added the inherited singleton derivative convention.

Convergence of a Dyson sum alone is not uniqueness, but the actual cited supplier proof 3.1 proves vector Volterra uniqueness in either time direction. Made the missing transfer explicit: conjugate the difference of two mild solutions by E(-t), iterate w=int B w, and let M(K|t-s|)^n/n! tend to zero. Also stated the inherited singleton derivative convention and corrected Teschl to autonomous evolution. The model and its outcome-law assertions are preserved.

L1 omitted omega nonzero and the initial-up preparation required by the population supplier. The Example already specifies initial |E> in clause (b), so its claimed inversion and bound are sound for that preparation. Restored those exact hypotheses in L1 and explicitly instantiated the compact-interval model and psi(s)=|E>=e_up in step 1.1. At resonance epsilon=x(1+3 mu E0 tau/hbar), giving the unchanged pulse bound (2+3pi)/100. No Example or physical-scope interface was changed.

The example did not declare a time interval containing its pulse evaluations.
